summary: Thurston County, WA Army lookout: 1930s wood tower, 1942 wood replacement, 1968 steel tower lost by 1994 (sources differ on how); now a turnaround on JBLM, no public access described.

facts.design: 100' wooden tower with 8'x8' cab (1930s); 50' wooden tower with 9'x9' AWS cab (1942); 112' all-steel tower (1968)
facts.status_note: Steel tower removed or destroyed by 1994 (sources differ); a 2013 visit found only a vehicle turnaround at the summit

staffing.status: Madeline Mullen staffed the lookout in summer 1975 (Willhite stories page); no other staffing found

access.note: Site lies on Joint Base Lewis-McChord, a military base; no public access described in the sources read

visit.trail_note: No tower remains to climb; the summit is a vehicle turnaround on JBLM (Willhite, 2013 photos)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says it was removed by 1994. firelookout.com and Forest Lookouts say it was destroyed in Army bombing or a training exercise in 1994. Willhite says some reports give the bombing account but base records show use after 1994. The story reports all three and does not choose one.
firelookout.com's heading reads 'R.I.P. 1942-1968', which conflicts with its own text placing the steel tower from 1968 until its destruction in 1994.

notes_for_editor: Fate of the steel tower is contested, and the story says so. The first tower is dated only to the 1930s in every source, so no 'built' event with a year is recorded. Staffing rests on one line in Willhite's stories page (summer 1975). Willhite's 2013 photos are the only description of the site today, and it is a second-hand account. Used 1 WebSearch and 5 page reads (FFLOS, firelookout.com, Forest Lookouts, Willhite, and the firelookout.org index).
